Bill.BriefDescription: Providing legal services for construction professionals involved in legal disputes concerning project permits.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to legal services for construction professionalsinvolved in legal disputes concerning project permits; adding a newsection to chapter 43.42 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature recognizes that thebuilding industry is a key driver of the state economy. Thelegislature further recognizes that the building industry singlehandedly kept the state economy afloat during the recent recession.The building industry, through singlefamily and multifamilyconstruction, generated one hundred two thousand three hundred fortyone direct jobs and an additional ten thousand five hundred eightytwospinoff jobs in Washington, more than any other industry. (2) The legislature recognizes that the governor recently enteredinto a contract with the Boeing company to ensure that the Boeingcompany will build the new 7E7 plant in Washington. Among otherprovisions, the governor granted the Boeing company state protectionagainst environmental lawsuits. (3) The legislature recognizes that developers and builders areconsistently sued by nogrowth activists to prevent legitimate p. 1 HB 3181development. The legislature finds that these suits stymie the stateeconomy and fetter thoughtful land use planning. Because the buildingindustry is the most important job creator and economic driver in thestate, the legislature extends the legal protections granted to theBoeing company to the entire building industry.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.42 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1)(a) For the purposes of this section, "constructionprofessional" means a land developer, builder, builder vendor,contractor, or subcontractor performing or furnishing the design,supervision, construction, or observation of the construction of anyimprovement to real property, whether operating as a sole proprietor,partnership, corporation, or other business entity. (b) "Project permit" or "project permit application" means any landuse or environmental permit or license required from a local governmentfor a project action, including but not limited to building permits,subdivisions, binding site plans, planned unit developments,conditional uses, shoreline substantial development permits, site planreview, permits or approvals required by critical area ordinances,site-specific rezones authorized by a comprehensive plan or subareaplan, but excluding the adoption or amendment of a comprehensive plan,subarea plan, or development regulations except as otherwisespecifically included in this subsection (1)(b). (2)(a) In the event that any party, other than the state or apolitical subdivision of the state, institutes any legal proceeding,including but not limited to proceedings under chapters 36.70C and90.58 RCW, against a construction professional regarding a projectpermit granted by the state or a political subdivision of the state,the office of the attorney general shall assume the entire defense ofthe proceedings, including all fees, costs, and expenses. (b) Without prior consultation with the construction professional,the office of the attorney general may not: (i) Make any settlement orcompromise of the legal proceedings; (ii) fail to pursue any availablelegal theory of avenue of appeal of any adverse judgment against whichthe construction professional believes is likely to be successful;(iii) elect to abandon any litigation or other legal proceedings under HB 3181 p. 2 (a) of this subsection; or (iv) take any action that would result inthe imposition of fees, charges, or costs upon the constructionprofessional.
